title: 1-Butanol + water, NRTL, 10 stages with a decanter on the condenser: the butanol-rich liquid is refluxed, the water-rich liquid is the distillate
purpose: A heterogeneous azeotropic column (milestone M2b): a water-rich feed (0.3 butanol, itself two liquids at its bubble point) enters stage 2; the vapour leaving the top stage is condensed and decanted; all of the butanol-rich liquid returns as reflux, all of the water-rich liquid leaves as the distillate, and 0.994 butanol leaves at the bottom. The decanter's two liquids are in liquid-liquid equilibrium at the condensate's bubble point. Two liquids also form on the stages above the stripping section.
method_choice: docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md rules 3 and 7: polar, below 10 bar, two liquids possible: NRTL (it describes two liquids), the default set of the pair (ChemSep databank, tier databank; its record states that it predicts two liquid phases), ideal-gas vapour.

specs.note: all of the liquid richer in 1-butanol is refluxed and all of the other liquid is the distillate; start_reflux_ratio is only the reference's first guess, not a specification

search.what: an open worked example of a heterogeneous azeotropic or decanter column with stage results
searched: The ChemSep Book, 2nd edition (2006, public domain), chapter 9 and section 13.7 (three-phase distillation): the method (an overall liquid with averaged K-values and enthalpy, section 13.7.2, eqs. 13.45-13.52), no example with numbers

a web search (n-butanol + water, decanter, column, stage results): an open batch heteroazeotropic study (OATAO / CORE, core.ac.uk/download/12042666.pdf; batch, not a continuous column) and an Aspen study of butanol recovery (Processes 10 (2022) 364, open access; its own property parameters, no stage table to compare)
the open sources of the earlier cases (DWSIM tutorials, NeqSim documentation): none with two liquids on the stages
search.result: none found with stage results; the independent reference is the reference

behaviour: the decanter's two liquids are the binary's liquid-liquid equilibrium at the heteroazeotropic temperature: the distillate is the water-rich liquid, the reflux the butanol-rich one (fixture stage 1 `decanter`)
the upper stages hold two liquids (the feed's stage among them), the stripping stages below one liquid; the bottoms are 0.99 or more 1-butanol (fixture)
the reflux is not a specification: it is the whole butanol-rich liquid, which follows from the vapour reaching the condenser
with phases "VL" the column is refused (PHASE_SPLIT or a decanter that needs two liquids), never solved with one liquid in the decanter
expected.branch: The reference's solution from its stated start (below the decanter, the stages start on the butanol-rich side, between the reflux liquid and the bottoms). Another solution exists that closes every balance with two liquids on every stage, so the start matters: an engine that finds it reports it for review.

engine_against_reference.why: Proposal 0015, Engineering basis: flows within 1e-6 relative of the independent MESH solution. Both solve the same equations to residuals of 1e-8 or less, so the difference is the solvers' convergence only.

balances_on_every_stage.why: Proposal 0015: every stage's balances closed to 1e-8. Material: |residual| / F; energy: |residual| / (F x 10 kJ/mol); summation and equilibrium are mole fractions.

agreement_with_data.note: The NRTL set (ChemSep, tier databank) sets the liquid-liquid split; its agreement with measured mutual solubilities is W1's work and not a test of the column.
